title: LLM.265: Video Codecs are Secretly Tensor Codecs
problem: LLM training and inference are increasingly bottlenecked by memory footprint and communication bandwidth for weights, activations, gradients, and KV cache, but existing tensor-compression methods are specialized for only one type of tensor and require custom hardware or software stacks. A unified, bandwidth-efficient compression mechanism applicable across all LLM tensor types is missing.
motivation: Video codec hardware (GPU video engines) has been refined for decades and is already present in commodity GPUs; if standard video codecs can exploit the statistical structure of LLM tensors, they offer an immediately deployable compression path with no GPU die-area addition.
method: LLM.265 repurposes existing GPU hardware video encoders/decoders (H.265/HEVC engines) as general-purpose tensor codecs. The key insight is that LLM tensors expose spatial and temporal statistical structure (smooth weight manifolds, slowly changing activations, correlated KV cache vectors) that codec stages — inter-frame prediction, DCT/transform coding, scalar quantization, and entropy coding via context-adaptive arithmetic coding — can exploit directly. The system maps tensor layouts to frame formats, applies intra/inter prediction to exploit tensor correlations, and uses entropy coding to compress residuals. Custom hardware extensions to the existing video engine improve tensor encoding/decoding throughput without major GPU architecture changes.
key_novelty: Reusing commodity GPU video codec hardware engines as unified tensor compressors for all LLM data types (weights, activations, gradients, KV cache), eliminating the need for specialized compression accelerators.
contributions: Demonstration that standard video codec stages (prediction, transform coding, quantization, entropy coding) effectively compress LLM weights, activations, gradients, and KV cache by exploiting their statistical structure
LLM.265 system that repurposes existing GPU video engines for tensor compression during LLM inference and distributed training
Proposed minimal hardware customizations to GPU video engines to improve tensor encode/decode throughput without major architecture changes
Unified compression approach that works across all LLM tensor types without per-type specialized methods

metrics.other: Compression effectiveness for weights, activations, gradients, KV cache not stated in abstract; throughput vs. baseline not stated

limitations: Quantitative compression ratios, throughput, and end-to-end speedup numbers are not reported in the abstract.
primary_theme: GPU video codec hardware repurposed as LLM tensor compressor
